newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Hydro says is on right track on profits.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Hydro says is on right track on profits.

text.p: Norwegian industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro ASA said on Monday weaker earnings in agricultural operations and higher calculated tax on oil and gas income burdened first-quarter profits.

The company booked a net income of 1.54 billion crowns ($219.3 million) in the first quarter, compared to 1.87 billion in the same period last year. Earnings per share were 6.70 crowns, down from 8.20 crowns.
Operating revenues, however, increased to 23.25 billion crowns from 21.38 billion in the first quarter of the previous year.
"After a slight setback at the end of 1996, we're pleased to say that Hydro is back on the right track," Chief Executive Officer Egil Mylebust said.
"However, the months ahead do hold some potential uncertainties in the world economy and in the market prospects for the major sectors in which Hydro operates."
Operating income was 3.15 billion, compared to 3.12 billion in the same year-ago period.
Hydro's Agriculture operations had an operating income of 856 million crowns, down from 889 million. Fertilizer sales were particularly high near the end of the quarter.
But earnings were weaker because of lower fertilizer prices and increased costs for raw materials, the company said in a statement.

First-quarter operating income for Oil and Gas was 1.92 billion, up from 1.50 billion, thanks primarily to a crude oil price of $21.4/bbl and higher production and lower operating costs per barrel than before.

The operating income for Light Metals fell to 396 million crowns from 689 million principally because of lower realised aluminium prices. But the operating income for aluminium showed significant improvement over the fourth quarter of 1996, the statement said.

Magnesium's operating income weakened compared to the first quarter of last year. While production of both primary and re-melted metal increased, realised prices remained lower than in the previous year, it said.

The Petrochemicals division's operating income shrank to 59 million crowns from 87 million. The weaker performance was due to lower caustic soda prices, increased raw materials costs as well as reduced production and sales due to the phase-in of new PVC production capacity in Norway and Britain. The new capacity will come on stream in the second quarter.
Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Leiv Nergaard said Hydro's accounts for the first three months confirmed that the company's operations were proving to be effective.

"The first quarter results also show that, in terms of the company's general development, not too much significance should be given to a single weak quarter, such as the fourth quarter of last year," Nergaard told Hydro's in-house magazine Profile.

He said the Hydro Plus improvement initiative, which was concluded at the end of 1996, provided a new platform for further growth. Results were already evident during 1996 in the form of a higher rate of investment and the acquisition of several businesses, he said.

"We're already seeing the impact of these changes in the first quarter, particularly in Agriculture. The Italian fertilizer operations which we acquired, coupled with the expansion of our marketing capacity in central Europe and on other continents, have compensated for the negative developments in the western European fertilizer markets, where low price has been a major factor," Nergaard said.
Commenting on the Oil and Gas Division, he said the rate of increase in production during the first quarter was stronger than can be expected for the remainder of the year.

"This current year will probably be exceptional with respect to the growth rate of petroleum production. We can expect production to begin rising again at a more significant rate next year," Nergaard said.
He said he was not entirely satisfied with the result of Light Metals although he noted it showed definite first-quarter improvement from the low in the fourth quarter of last year.

He said the sector had to deal with several unexpected situations last year, including a sharp reduction in electric power production caused by the abnormally low levels of precipitation in Norway. This had a negative impact on the results of Hydro Energy, but the electric power situation appeared to have returned to normal during the first quarter. ($ = 7.021 Norwegian Crowns)
